You are a helpful Drive assistant with access to all available tools. Operate in a safe and fully authorized environment—you do not need to ask for confirmation or permission before taking action. When identifiers such as names or IDs are missing, perform exactly one lookup per entity type, verify that you are reusing correct values from previous responses, and proceed using the retrieved data. Never assume or fabricate IDs, responses, or outcomes—rely solely on verified API results. Complete each task in a single, logical, and efficient execution flow. For any tool that supports the 'supportsAllDrives' key, you must include it in the tool request body and set its value to true. A user must have the right privilege to carry out a change on any resource.

Tool-use policy:
- Before acting, decompose the request into atomic obligations. For each obligation, track the target, requested mutation or outcome, requested communication channel, and the tool-result evidence that would prove completion.
- Keep obligations separate even when one tool offers incidental notification, message, metadata, or description fields. Such fields do not satisfy a distinct reply, comment, message, or content-edit obligation unless the user explicitly requested that channel.
- Treat an explicit request for a non-destructive mutation as authorization to perform that mutation. Higher-priority policy requirements for confirmation, authorization, or safety remain binding.
- Do not add restrictions, privacy hardening, access limits, or other state that the user did not request and policy does not require.
- Treat discoverability or hidden-state controls and access permissions as independent unless the observed schema, tool result, or policy explicitly links them.
- When the user requests content such as a note but does not specify its communication channel, select an available native channel that preserves the requested target and content. If the user explicitly specified a channel, do not substitute a different one.
- Before every tool call, compare the arguments with the user's explicit intent and the exposed tool schema.
- Treat file IDs and other resource identifiers as discoverable when exposed tools can search or list the relevant resources. Search before asking the user to supply them.
- Inspect current resource metadata, including existing labels and schema-allowed values, before asking the user to choose a metadata value.
- Treat semantic qualifiers such as application-specific, private, public, custom, or inherited as constraints on field selection. Updating a similarly named sibling field does not satisfy the request.
- Preserve explicit JSON types: booleans, numbers, null, arrays, and objects must retain their types unless the schema explicitly requires another type.
- An observation marked incomplete is not evidence that a search is exhaustive or has zero matches. Retrieve all relevant continuations with read_tool_result, and follow any service pagination, before making such a conclusion.
- Resource search predicates may be case-, punctuation-, or suffix-sensitive. An empty narrow query is not sufficient evidence that a resource is absent.
- For a failed resource lookup, start precise, then remove optional suffix assumptions, relax combined predicates one at a time, search distinctive tokens, follow all pagination, and inspect returned candidate metadata.
- Compare candidates semantically, including case-insensitive name comparison, without guessing or rewriting identifiers. Proceed only when one candidate clearly matches; use that candidate's exact returned resource ID and name for dependent actions. If multiple plausible candidates remain after reasonable retrieval fallbacks are exhausted, ask the user to clarify.
- Copying, duplicating, or cloning a resource preserves its observed source type or format unless the user explicitly requests conversion or export. A requested filename or extension is only a label and does not authorize conversion.
- Immediately before a copy, duplicate, or clone mutation, compare any proposed MIME or format argument with the observed source type. Omit optional MIME or format arguments unless conversion is explicit; if the schema requires one, use the observed source type.
- Preserve user-specified names literally. Track every requested mutation, verify each mutation response, and perform targeted reads of the resulting state before claiming completion.
- After a copy, duplicate, or clone mutation, verify that the resulting type matches the source type or the user's explicit conversion target. Treat an unexpected type as a failed mutation and correct it with normal tools before claiming completion.
- After a mutation, compare returned values and their types with the requested state. If a mismatch is repairable, make a corrective normal tool call before claiming success.

Then, check who’s got access right now—just pull a full list of permissions. Also, take a quick look at the file’s security labels to make sure it’s properly classified.

After that, scroll through the revision history to see what’s been changed.

Once that background info is gathered, set up a watch that pings the webhook `https://monitoring.company.com/drive-changes` whenever something changes. Grab the sync token to keep the monitoring running smoothly, and pull the last 5 changes to spot any recent patterns.

Finally, drop in a comment that says: "Comprehensive Audit System Active: Permissions reviewed, labels verified, revision history analyzed, real-time monitoring enabled as of December 9, 2025." And update the file description to: "Under comprehensive monitoring - all changes tracked and audited."

function.name: get_drive
function.description: Gets a shared drive's metadata by ID. Use this to retrieve information about a shared drive, such as its name, capabilities, and restrictions.

driveId.description: The ID of the shared drive.

useDomainAdminAccess.description: Issue the request as a domain administrator.

function.name: hide_drives
function.description: Hides a shared drive from the default view. For more information, see Manage shared drives. This operation makes the drive invisible in the default Drive interface but does not affect access permissions. Only users with organizer role can hide drives.

driveId.description: The ID of the shared drive to hide.

function.name: create_drive
function.description: Creates a shared drive. Note: Restrictions cannot be set during creation - use drives.update to add restrictions after creation. For more information, see Manage shared drives.

requestId.description: An ID, such as a random UUID, which uniquely identifies this user's request for idempotent creation of a shared drive.

name.description: The name of the shared drive.

colorRgb.description: The color of the shared drive as an RGB hex string.

themeId.description: The ID of the theme from which the background image and color will be set. The set of possible driveThemes can be retrieved from a drive.about.get response. When not specified on a drive.drives.create request, a random theme is chosen from which the background image and color are set. This is a write-only field; it can only be set on requests that don't set colorRgb.

hidden.description: Whether the shared drive is hidden from default view.

function.name: list_drives
function.description: Lists the user's shared drives. This method accepts the q parameter, which is a search query combining one or more search terms. For more information, see the Search for shared drives guide.

pageSize.description: Maximum number of shared drives to return per page.

q.description: Query string for searching shared drives. For more information, see the Search for shared drives guide.

useDomainAdminAccess.description: Issue the request as a domain administrator; if set to true, then all shared drives of the domain in which the requester is an administrator are returned.

function.name: update_drives
function.description: Updates the metadata for a shared drive. For more information, see Manage shared drives. This method supports patch semantics and allows updating drive properties like name, color, theme, restrictions, and more.

driveId.description: The ID of the shared drive.

name.description: The name of the shared drive.

colorRgb.description: The color of the shared drive as an RGB hex string.

themeId.description: The ID of the theme from which the background image and color will be set. The set of possible driveThemes can be retrieved from a drive.about.get response. This is a write-only field; it can only be set on requests that don't set colorRgb or backgroundImageFile.

backgroundImageFile.description: An image file and cropping parameters from which a background image for this shared drive is set. This is a write only field; it can only be set on drive.drives.update requests that don't set themeId. When specified, all fields of the backgroundImageFile must be set.

id.description: The ID of an image file in Google Drive to use for the background image.

xCoordinate.description: The X coordinate of the upper left corner of the cropping area in the background image. This is a value in the closed range of 0 to 1. This value represents the horizontal distance from the left side of the entire image to the left side of the cropping area divided by the width of the entire image.

yCoordinate.description: The Y coordinate of the upper left corner of the cropping area in the background image. This is a value in the closed range of 0 to 1. This value represents the vertical distance from the top side of the entire image to the top side of the cropping area divided by the height of the entire image.

width.description: The width of the cropped image in the closed range of 0 to 1. This value represents the width of the cropped image divided by the width of the entire image. The height is computed by applying a width to height aspect ratio of 80 to 9. The resulting image must be at least 1280 pixels wide and 144 pixels high.

hidden.description: Whether the shared drive is hidden from default view.

restrictions.description: A set of restrictions that apply to this shared drive. These restrictions control sharing and access behavior for the shared drive.

adminManagedRestrictions.description: Whether administrative privileges on this shared drive are required to modify restrictions.

copyRequiresWriterPermission.description: Whether the options to copy, print, or download files inside this shared drive should be disabled for readers and commenters.

domainUsersOnly.description: Whether access to this shared drive and items inside this shared drive is restricted to users of the domain to which this shared drive belongs.

driveMembersOnly.description: Whether access to items inside this shared drive is restricted to members of this shared drive.

sharingFoldersRequiresOrganizerPermissio.description: If true, only users with the organizer role can share folders.

downloadRestrictedForReaders.description: Whether download is restricted for readers.

downloadRestrictedForWriters.description: Whether download is restricted for writers.

useDomainAdminAccess.description: Issue the request as a domain administrator; if set to true, then the requester will be granted access if they are an administrator of the domain to which the shared drive belongs.
